title: First-run telemetry playbook — screenshot and canvas assets for observability quickstart
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Produce a cohesive, reusable set of visual assets for the Observability quickstart and release notes that show latency, cost-per-token, and trace views across typical Redwood usage patterns. Deliverables include high-resolution PNG/JPEG screenshots, vector canvases for docs, annotated callout overlays, mobile/responsive variants, and an A/B set for 'detailed' vs 'compact' dashboard modes. Screenshots must be anonymized (no customer IDs), deterministic (use seeded demo data), and optimized for both light and dark themes. Primary artboards: 1) Latency distribution heatmap with percentile overlays and hover state callout; 2) Cost-per-token timeline with per-route breakout and currency formatting; 3) Trace waterfall view showing span durations, service labels, and a zoomed-in KV cache miss example; 4) Combined snapshot that fits hero banner sizes for docs (1200x480) and marketplace tiles (640x320). Provide Figma page with named components and an export QA checklist. Include brief copy snippets for docs and release changelog that explain what each screenshot demonstrates (what to look for, common explanations for anomalies).
acceptance_criteria: All screenshot variants exported in light and dark themes at required resolutions: hero (1200x480), docs inline (900x320), marketplace thumbnail (640x320), mobile (375x812)
Assets are anonymized and use seeded demo workloads — no real org names or tokens visible
Annotated overlays (callouts) exist for each image explaining the key metric and where to find it in the Console
Figma file contains a components page with export-ready frames and a naming convention guide
Design review approved by PM and Eng; handoff ticket for engineering to bake demo data and deterministic timestamps created
